decisive_items: a 10-cm calcified gallbladder wall invading liver segments 4 and 5
a distended gallbladder with poor delineation of the posterior wall, appearing large, solid, and heterogeneous with posterior dense shadowing and calcific components
enlarged coeliac, peri-pancreatic, and para-aortic lymph nodes
response.rationale: The imaging features of a calcified gallbladder wall mass invading the liver, with regional lymphadenopathy and pulmonary nodules, point to primary gallbladder cancer with metastatic spread. Cholangiocarcinoma is less likely because the common bile duct was normal in calibre and there was no intrahepatic duct dilatation, while metastatic disease is a consequence rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Cholangiocarcinoma is unsupported by the normal common bile duct calibre and absence of intrahepatic duct dilatation; the dominant abnormality is a calcified gallbladder wall mass invading the liver.
Metastatic disease describes the spread of the malignancy but not the primary diagnosis; the gallbladder origin is clearly identified on imaging.
